'''''Asparagus acutifolius''''', common name '''wild asparagus''', is an evergreen [[perennial]] plant belonging to the genus ''[[Asparagus]]''. The [[Binomial nomenclature|specific epithet]], {{lang|la|acutifolius}} is derived from [[Latin]] {{lang|la|acutus}} (pointed, acute), and {{lang|la|-folius}} (-leaved), and refers to the characteristic shape of the leaves, a quite common feature in the typical plants of the Mediterranean.<ref name="Eggli Newton 2004">{{cite book
| last1        = Eggli
| first1       = Urs

== Description ==
''Asparagus acutifolius'' reaches on average {{convert|30|-|70|cm}} of height. The stems have much-branched feathery foliage. The "leaves" are in fact needle-like [[Aerial stem modification|modified stems]]. The flowers are bell-shaped and in small clusters, greenish-white to yellowish, {{convert|4.5|-|5.5|mm}} long. The flowers are [[dioecious]] (on each plant they are only female or male). In some Mediterranean regions flowering occurs in late summer from August through September, often after heavy storms. In this case the small green berries, of {{convert|5|-|6|mm}} in diameter, are fully ripe in winter.

== Distribution ==
This species is present throughout the [[Mediterranean Basin]].

== Habitat ==
These plants grow near woods and in uncultivated places, on dry and sunny soil. They can be found at an altitude of {{convert|0|-|1300|m}} above sea level.

== Uses ==
Shoots are collected in the spring along the Croatian coast and islands and eaten in risottos and fried with scrambled eggs.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://triciaannemitchell.com/2013/03/24/the-wild-asparagus-of-croatia-a-foraging-trip-lunch-in-the-dalmatian-countryside/ | title=Foraging for Wild Asparagus in Croatia's Dalmatian Countryside | date=24 March 2013 }}</ref><ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.inforovinj.com/eng/rovinj/flora-fauna/flora/sparoga/asparagus.asp | title=The wild asparagus (Asparagus acutifolius) }}</ref>
